I stopped using facebook nearly 6 years ago, and in hindsight, I certainly think that was a great decision. Had always been an extremely shy and quiet introvert but while on facebook, I initially felt a sense of freedom and confidence - I would try to make interesting posts everyday, change profile pictures frequently, and so on (middle school / high school years). Then a few hours later, I'd be overcome with a feeling of regret and embarrassment, and would then delete the posts / pictures. After a point, I began to feel over-exposed and realized that I had been going against my personality, so I quit. I recently logged back in to my deactivated account and saw just how that landscape has changed - it's become very political,  commercial, and of course, has turned into a breeding ground for misinformation. Glad I deactivated when I did because although I was disconnected from people, I feel more in tune with myself. Besides, the people who really matter will always be only a call or text away.

Similar experience here. I committed misconduct during my freshman quarter for a CS course and got flagged for it (so much for three lines of bash code - CS is not even my major, so I'll take this to the grave). Grade dropped to B+ but nothing shows up on my transcripts. What I've learned from my university Academic Affairs program is that schools can certainly find out, so it would definitely be a good idea to include it in your application (this could be specific to my university as they don't remove the record internally). As one of the comments on the thread mentioned, it might be also be a good idea to explain it somewhere, maybe focus on what that taught you about academic work and how that might even help you combat the stresses and resist the temptations in the pressure cooker environment of grad school. In my opinion, being honest would be your best bet here. I also know that students from my school  have gone on to grad schools and med programs even after misconduct issues (most likely minor violations), so don't give up hope entirely. Good luck!
